content:
Let  

\[
AB =200,\qquad AC =225,\qquad BC =x .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 1.  The point \(D\)

Since \(AD\) bisects \(\angle BAC\),

\[
\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{AB}{AC}=\frac{200}{225}=\frac{8}{9}.
\]

Hence there is a positive number \(k\) such that  

\[
BD=8k,\qquad DC=9k,\qquad BC=17k .
\]

Because \(BD\) and \(DC\) are integers, \(k\) must be an integer (otherwise
the denominators would have to divide both 8 and 9, impossible).
Thus

\[
BC=17k\qquad(k\in\mathbb Z_{>0}).
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 2.  The circle \(\omega\)

\(\omega\) passes through \(A\) and is tangent to \(BC\) at \(D\).
For any point outside the circle, the power of the point equals the
product of the distances to the two intersection points of any secant
through that point with the circle.

* For \(B\): the secant \(BA\) meets the circle at \(A\) and at \(E\).

\[
BE\cdot BA = BD^{2}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
BE=\frac{BD^{2}}{BA}=\frac{(8k)^{2}}{200}= \frac{8k^{2}}{25}.
\]

Hence  

\[
AE=AB-BE=200-\frac{8k^{2}}{25}. \tag{1}
\]

* For \(C\): the secant \(CA\) meets the circle at \(A\) and at \(F\).

\[
CF\cdot CA = CD^{2}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
CF=\frac{CD^{2}}{CA}=\frac{(9k)^{2}}{225}= \frac{9k^{2}}{25}.
\]

Thus  

\[
AF=AC-CF =225-\frac{9k^{2}}{25}. \tag{2}
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 3.  Integral conditions

We are given that

\[
AE,\ AF,\ BD,\ CD\ \text{are positive integers}.
\]

The integrality of \(BD\) and \(CD\) has already forced \(k\) to be an
integer.  
For \(AE\) and \(AF\) to be integers, the fractions in (1) and (2)
must be integral.  
Since \(\gcd(8,25)=\gcd(9,25)=1\), this happens only when

\[
k^{2}\text{ is a multiple of }25\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad k=5m,
\]

with \(m\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).

Substituting \(k=5m\),

\[
BD=40m, \qquad CD=45m,\qquad BC=85m .
\]

Now

\[
AE=200-\frac{8(25m^{2})}{25}=200-8m^{2},
\]
\[
AF=225-\frac{9(25m^{2})}{25}=225-9m^{2}.
\]

Both must be positive, so

\[
8m^{2}<200\quad\text{and}\quad 9m^{2}<225
\Longrightarrow m^{2}<25\Longrightarrow m\le4 .
\]

Thus \(m=1,2,3,4\).

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 4.  Corresponding values of \(BC\)

For each admissible \(m\),

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
m & BC=85m & \text{Check triangle inequalities} \\ \hline
1 & 85   & \text{All satisfied} \\
2 & 170  & \text{All satisfied} \\
3 & 255  & \text{All satisfied} \\
4 & 340  & \text{All satisfied}
\end{array}
\]

All four lengths satisfy the triangle inequalities
(\(200+225>BC\), etc.) and give integer values of \(AE,\ AF\).
Hence all four are valid.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
### 5.  Sum of all possible \(BC\)

\[
85+170+255+340 = 850 .
\]

--------------------------------------------------------------------
\[
\boxed{850}
\]
